description: Complete typed assessments retained separately from the concise public TD; applicability is not satisfaction.

assessments.rationale: Implement ONVIF Network Interface Specification Set 2.4 or later; neither a schema version nor a device-advertised profile scope proves this.

Implemented functions follow their referenced native service specifications. This ledger enumerates explicit profile obligations and selected inherited wire invariants, not every requirement of every referenced service document.
Apply feature and function levels independently. Conditional feature support includes proprietary functionality; an M function inside that feature is required only in the enclosing scope.
Apply the Profile Mandatory Features minimum to this role; later function-level conditions and optional entries remain distinct.
Implement HTTP Digest according to Core. A TD security declaration or a successful unauthenticated request is not authentication evidence.
Return MaxPullPoints >= 2 in Event GetServiceCapabilities. The literal integer threshold is two; omission is not a known zero.

Implement the native XPath search-filter dialect, its namespaces and search scope; a string-valued schema alone does not implement filtering.

Execute native replay using session-correlated RTSP PLAY and absolute Range: clock= UTC bounds. Open/closed ranges, Scale direction and Rate-Control remain native runtime contracts, not synthetic SOAP inputs.
Support/use Require: onvif-replay in native RTSP SETUP and PLAY. URI acquisition is not replay execution.
Keep a missing-recording fault (NoRecording), unsupported StreamSetup, RTSP errors and transport/authentication failures distinguishable; never replace them with an empty successful stream.

Produce/understand the replay RTP extension on each access unit's first packet: original-capture NTP time, C clean point, E recording-section end, D discontinuity, reserved-zero bits and the low byte of PLAY CSeq. Preserve the T terminal hint without upgrading its recommendation to a mandatory flag.

Reverse replay is optional. When implemented, negotiate native support and use negative Scale; accept -1.0 and preserve reverse GOP/discontinuity and decreasing clock-range semantics. Do not infer reverse support from the URI.

Section 9 is mandatory for devices and feature-dependent for clients; do not transfer a device requirement to a client without its own gate.
Provide at least one complete recording-source branch. Both on-board sourcing and receiver sourcing are allowed; support of one isolated configuration operation is not a complete branch.
CreateRecordingJob returns both JobToken and the configuration actually used by the device. Preserve an adjusted returned configuration rather than echoing the requested one.
Idle and Active are requested modes. Active means attempt reception, not proof that data transfers; obtain actual aggregate/source/track state using GetRecordingJobState.
Retain non-negative job priority and per-track arbitration: highest priority wins, and a same-priority tie uses the latest activation. A flat boolean recording property cannot replace this behavior.
Retain typed Profile versus Receiver source references, parent recording identity and SourceTag-to-Destination track routing. SourceToken and AutoCreateReceiver have native conditional semantics.

Preserve each recording token, its configuration and its nested Tracks/Track entries. A track token is unique only inside its recording; resource identity also includes endpoint and service, never a globally flattened TrackToken.
